candidate_relations.reason: The histopathology describes intravascular papillary structures with hyaline globules in endothelial cells, which can overlap with Dabska tumor morphology. However, the IHC profile is critical: D2-40 (podoplanin) is negative and HHV-8 is negative, ruling out lymphatic differentiation and Kaposi sarcoma. Dabska tumor characteristically shows D2-40 positivity reflecting its lymphatic endothelial origin. The CD31+/D2-40- profile, benign clinical behavior, well-circumscribed architecture, and PAS-positive hyaline globules in a middle-aged man are consistent with papillary hemangioma (a benign blood vascular tumor), not Dabska tumor. The candidate asserts an incompatible malignant/lymphatic subtype.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Dabska tumor (papillary intralymphatic angioendothelioma) is a distinct low-grade malignant vascular neoplasm with lymphatic differentiation, whereas the reference is papillary hemangioma, a benign vascular tumor

case_quality_flags: Morphologic overlap between papillary hemangioma and Dabska tumor acknowledged; IHC (D2-40 negativity) is the decisive discriminator favoring the reference diagnosis
